title: Goje One-String Fiddle
summary: The goje, or goge, is a one-string bowed fiddle of the Hausa lands of northern Nigeria and Niger. A gourd body covered with skin carries a single horsehair string, and the bow slides along it as the fingers stop the string at different points.
howToPlay: The top row has six lanes, from the open string to the high stop; the lower row has two drum sounds.
Notes travel toward a line at the bottom; strike the lane just as a note arrives.
Start with the slow melody, then play the fiddle line between the low and high drum strokes.
The quick runs finish the set: slide through the stops and keep the pulse.
rules: One string gives every note: each stop shortens it to a higher pitch, from the open string up to the high stop.
A stroke within a hair of the note is perfect, a near one is good, and a missed one scores nothing.
An extra stroke while a song is running costs a few points.
Each song plays twice; three stars need roughly nine notes in ten on time.
Bowing glides and slides between notes are not shown; each stop sounds at a fixed pitch.
heritageNote: The goje is played by Hausa musicians in Nigeria and Niger, often to accompany singers who recount family histories and local news. Players make the instrument from a gourd, skin and horsehair and keep their own style of playing.
